'''''Coleonema pulchellum''''', commonly known as '''confetti bush''', '''buchu''', '''diosma''' or ''' breath of heaven''', is a shrub which is [[endemic]] to the [[Cape Provinces]] of [[South Africa]].<ref name=pa>{{cite web|title=''Coleonema pulchellum''|url=http://www.plantzafrica.com/plantcd/coleonpulchell.htm|work=PlantZAfrica.com|publisher=South African National Biodiversity Institute|accessdate=5 January 2013}}</ref><ref name=burke/> 

==Description==
[[File:Coleonema pulchellum 1c.JPG|thumb|220px|A flowering shrub|left]]
It is woody, evergreen and rather dense shrub that is erect in posture that grows to between {{convert|0.8|and|1.6|m}} high. It forms a single stem at the base, from where numerous thin and erect branches grow. The aromatic leaves are like needles and are 4 to 5 times longer (8-10 mm) than they are wide (0.8 mm). The [[petiole (botany)|petiole]] is 1 mm long. The dwarf variety 'Dwarf Pink' grows between {{convert|0.6|and|0.9|m}}.

The flowers are solitary, terminal in short axillary twigs or in small twigs, often dense towards the top of the branches. They are pink, often white, and star-shaped (7 to 8 mm in diameter), with 5 oval [[petal]]s, 5.0-5.7 mm long, each marked with a distinctive central vein. The entire shrub will be covered in pink flowers from May to October, attracting bees, butterflies and other insects. The fruit is made up of a 5-chamber [[Capsule (fruit)|capsule]], dotted with glands. There is a shiny black seed in each chamber.<ref name=pa/>

==Taxonomy==
The species was formally described in 1981 in the ''Journal of South African Botany''.<ref name=APNI>{{cite web 
|url=http://www.anbg.gov.au/cgi-bin/apni?TAXON_NAME=Coleonema+pulchellum|title=''Coleonema pulchellum'' |accessdate=5 January 2013 |work= [[Australian Plant Name Index]] (APNI), IBIS database|publisher = Centre for Plant Biodiversity Research, Australian Government, Canberra}}</ref> Prior to this, plants in cultivation had been erroneously identified as ''[[Coleonema pulchrum]]''.<ref name=burke/>

The species is naturalised in [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]], Australia.<ref name=APNI/>

==Cultivars==
* 'Compactum' ('Nanum') — dwarf pink flowering form growing to 1m
*'Rubrum' ('Red Form') — red flowering form
*'Sunset Gold' — dwarf form with golden foliage to 75 cm high <ref name=burke>{{cite web|title=Diosma|publisher=Burke's Backyard|url=http://www.burkesbackyard.com.au/1998/archives/26/in_the_garden/flowering_plants_and_shrubs/diosma|accessdate=5 January 2013}}</ref>
*'Album' — white flowering variant
